chunks: My father (RA) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Yazid narrated from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rubay ibn Abd Allah, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu Abd Allah (AS) saying:
Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, cannot be described. Zurarah said: Abu Ja'far (AS) said: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, cannot be described,
And they did not appraise Allah with true appraisal.
So whatever attribute of power they assign to Him, He is greater than that.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that Allah cannot be described by power?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* elucidates the Shia doctrine of divine incomparability (*tanzih*) by arguing that attributing 'power' to Allah implies a limitation, as any created concept of power is inherently lesser than His infinite essence. By citing the verse 'And they did not appraise Allah with true appraisal,' the Imams emphasize that human language cannot encapsulate the absolute magnitude of the Divine, a key tenet in Shia kalam to prevent anthropomorphism.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 6. My father (RA) related us that Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said: Ya`qub ibn Yazid said, on the authority of Hammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of Rub`I ibn `Abd Allah, on the authority of al-Fudayl ibn Yasar that I heard Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) that “Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, cannot be described.” Zurarah said: Abu Ja`far al-Baqir (AS) said: “Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, cannot be described.
And how could He be described when He has said in his Book:
And they do not assign to Allah the attributes due to Him
? Thus, whatever they assign Him, He is greater than that.”
